For a while, the future of foldable smartphones—whether clamshell or book-style—remained unclear, but at least for now, the book-style foldable is clearly the winner.

Samsung's eighth-generation foldable phone uses this design, the rumored iPhone Ultra is also expected to follow suit, and leaked images of the Xiaomi 18 Fold are riding the same wave…

Foldable smartphones mainly come in two forms, commonly known as clamshell and book-style.

The clamshell design essentially folds a traditional smartphone into a thicker device with half the height, offering a standard-sized screen in a more portable form factor. The Motorola Razr is one example, with its design also echoing the style that the company first promoted back in 2004.

The book-style design (increasingly called that for obvious reasons) unfolds a more square-shaped device into something the size of a small tablet (like the iPad mini). This is exactly the design Apple plans to unveil next month.

Samsung has popularized this design with its Galaxy Z Fold series, having just launched the eighth-generation model last month.

Xiaomi is now also preparing to join the fray with the 18 Fold, whose camera module design is strikingly similar to the rumored iPhone Ultra. Weibo user Peter shared two photos (above), suspecting they are engineering prototypes rather than actual production models.

Our sister site 9to5Google notes that this deep cherry color appears to be inspired by one of the rumored color options for the iPhone 18 Pro.
